reports.title: Volkswirtschaftliche Gesamtrechnung (VGR FL)
reports.description: Liechtenstein's own national accounts — confirmed to exist as a distinct publication despite the customs and currency union with Switzerland — citing ESVG 2010 (ESA 2010) as its methodological basis.

entries.covers: Volkswirtschaftliche Gesamtrechnung 2024 (Berichtsjahr 2024)

release_schedule.note: The Amt für Statistik Liechtenstein's publication archive (filtered to topic 'Volkswirtschaftliche Gesamtrechnungen') shows this full VGR FL report has been released every year in late November for at least the last four editions: VGR 2020 published 25.11.2022, VGR 2021 published 28.11.2023, VGR 2022 published 28.11.2024, VGR 2023 published 28.11.2025 (each entry tagged 'erscheint jährlich' / published annually, and each report's own metadata footer states 'Erscheinungsweise: jährlich'). There is roughly a 2-year lag between the report year covered and the publication date (e.g. the 2023-data edition appeared in Nov 2025). No exact day-of-month rule is stated, only the observed late-November clustering (25th-28th), so the next edition (covering report year 2024) is projected for November 2026 at month precision rather than an exact day. Note: this office also separately publishes a faster preliminary 'Schätzrechnung Bruttoinlandsprodukt' (GDP flash estimate) each March, which is a distinct product from this full VGR FL report and is not what's being scheduled here.

Quarterly national accounts (ESA 2010) follow a two-stage cycle per quarter: a 'flash estimate' press release ~1 month after quarter-end, followed by the detailed 'Quarterly Gross domestic product of the Republic of Serbia' statistical release ~2 months after quarter-end. reports.title: Échelle mobile des salaires (automatic wage indexation)
reports.description: Luxembourg's statutory automatic wage-indexation mechanism (Loi du 25 mars 2015), which adjusts wages and salaries periodically whenever STATEC's published consumer price index crosses a defined threshold.

entries.covers: Next automatic wage indexation tranche (déclenchement de l'échelle mobile des salaires)

release_schedule.rule: L'échelle mobile des salaires se déclenche automatiquement lorsque la moyenne mobile semestrielle de l'indice national des prix à la consommation dépasse de 2,5 % son niveau au précédent déclenchement (loi modifiée du 27 mai 1975 concernant l'échelle mobile des salaires et des traitements). La dernière tranche est intervenue le 1er juin 2026 (indice 992,24, contre 968,04 précédemment).
release_schedule.note: This is not a scheduled publication but an automatic trigger: whenever the 6-month moving average of Luxembourg's CPI exceeds the level at the previous trigger by 2.5%, wages/pensions/social parameters are indexed +2.5%. STATEC's central forecast (June 2026 report, reaffirmed 24 June 2026) projects the next trigger in Q2 2027, with no second 2026 tranche expected given ~2.2% inflation for 2026 and the 'Resilienzpak 2026' energy-price-capping measures. STATEC itself flags this could move earlier (as early as Q3 2026) if inflation accelerates (e.g., from an oil-price shock), so the Q2 2027 date is a rolling forecast, not a fixed date.

_dropped.why: Statbel itself makes no direct statement that it compiles national accounts under ESA 2010 — searches on statbel.fgov.be for 'SEC 2010' / 'ESA 2010' / 'comptes nationaux' returned nothing. Belgian national accounts are actually produced by the Institut des comptes nationaux, housed at the National Bank of Belgium, which DOES use binding language ('établis selon les prescrits du SEC 2010'). See the round-7 slice, where the correct source (NBB/ICN) is used instead.
